newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty softens vs basket, O/N depos inch up.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty softens vs basket, O/N depos inch up.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed a touch weaker against the basket of currencies after on a early currency-buying trend caused by a strong dollar and small orders from importers, dealers said.
The zloty closed at 1.70/1.65 pct from the trading band centre, softer than Wedesday's close at 1.75/1.70 percent from parity but trade was very light.
"Activity was light today and after a morning dollar-buying trend, trading basically came to a halt," said Leszek Szafranek, forex dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
The zloty was at 2.7480/90 per dollar, flat from 2.7480/90 on Wednesday and at 1.8538/49 per mark, down from 1.8496/07.

Dealers said the zloty was likely to stay subdued between 1.5 and 1.8 percent from the trading band centre in the near-term as most large transactions now likely take place at the post-trade fixing session.
The money market remained strapped for cash on Thursday and overnight rates inched up to 19.2/19.5 percent at close from 19.0/19.45 percent at 0630 GMT in thin trade, dealers said.
Tomorrow/next rates were at 19.2/19.55 percent, barely changed from 19.1/19.6 percent at opening.
Analysts said the present row in Poland's ruling coalition had no effect on the market, but that if the conflict yields early parliamentary polls the situation would change.
"It had nearly no effect on the market so far, but we are watching it closely," said one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw.

Analysts said a 1.7 percent in broad money supply in August, following a 2.3 percent rise in July, was in line with analyst expectations but that a quick rise in credit action could stir up inflation in the fourth quarter.
Broad money supply grew 16.7 percent in the January-August period against 20.9 percent in the same period of last year. @
They said continued slow growth of food prices, which rose just 0.1 percent from the July 20-30 period to August 20-30 could increase make the possibility of an interest rate cut as early in October.
